site.title: Go ports of JavaScript tooling
site.subtitle: npm packages rebuilt in Go, verified against the originals
site.intro: Each project below is a Go implementation of a JavaScript/npm library or tool. None of them are 'inspired by' rewrites: every one carries a parity harness that runs the real npm package as the oracle and fails when the Go output differs. The numbers on this page are the gate results from those harnesses.

highlight.name: eslint-go
highlight.tagline: ESLint's Linter pipeline in Go — parses with a Go parser, runs real ESLint rules, and its CLI output is byte-identical to eslint 8.57
points: Text is parsed in-process by espree-go (a Go port of espree) — no Node runtime, no subprocess.
46 ported rules (no-undef, no-unused-vars, prefer-const, semi, quotes, …) run over one traversal, with eslint-scope-go scope analysis behind them, gated by 2,437 oracle cases.
`eslint-go --format stylish src` produces the same bytes as `eslint --format stylish src`: colours, columns, exit codes and the files rewritten by --fix.
Message objects match field for field — including suggestions, fix ranges, and UTF-16 code-unit columns on non-ASCII input.
21 leaf packages were ported first (espree, acorn, estraverse, esquery, eslint-scope, …) and are composing here.

method.title: How a port is verified
steps: Vendor the original npm package next to the Go code — the oracle, not a reference to read.
Build a corpus of real inputs (valid, invalid, edge, non-ASCII) and a driver that runs the original package over it.
Run the same corpus through the Go implementation and diff the results: full JSON ASTs for parsers, message objects for linters, byte-for-byte output for code generators and fixers.
Treat any difference as a bug in the port. When the difference is caused by the original's own behaviour, encode that behaviour deliberately and say so in the README.
Commit only when the harness reports zero mismatches, and keep the number in the repo's README so it can be re-checked.
